pageCache.pageTitle: Mr Gary Peace – The Island Free School
pageCache.text:
(01983) 857641
Monday – Friday: 8am to 4:30pm
Mr Gary Peace
Chair of Governors, Child Protection Governor
A businessman with a background in the Met Police, now based on the Island with his family.
After leaving school, Gary became an engineering apprentice at the University of Sussex, where he also worked as a Mechanical Engineering Technician. In 1992, he gained an HNC in Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering (Design) from Brighton Polytechnic.
In 1994 he joined the Metropolitan Police Service in London where he served for 19 years, predominantly as a Detective in a variety of departments and squads. When he left in 2013, to set up his own company, he was Scotland Yard’s sole Network Investigator for all professional standards and anti-corruption investigations.
Gary and his family now live on the Island where he is an independent consultant and Managing Director of ESID Limited, based at the Innovation Centre in Newport. His company provide services in the fields of e-discovery, information security, computer forensics and data recovery, and they have a growing number of public and private sector clients across the country.
In May 2017, Gary was elected the Councillor for Ventnor West.
Gary is a keen sailor and qualified yachtmaster as well as a qualified pilot and Civilian Gliding Instructor RAF VR(T), who has taught Air Cadets to fly solo in gliders.
"Gary has an extraordinary skill set, ranging from investigating high tech crimes to flying planes. His expertise and commitment to education is impressive."
"With children of school age, my wife and I were becoming increasingly concerned with the quality of provision of senior school education on the Island. I see The Island Free School as the ‘standard bearer’, for a better and brighter future, for all of our children. This is why I am so enthusiastic about getting involved and helping the school to achieve the aspirations and the vision of its founders"

Mr John Bagshawe
Governor
John moved to the Island at the beginning of 2017. He had intended to stay in Kent where he had lived all his life, but feels that this move to the island was meant to be after buying a house at auction, which he didn’t expect to secure! He was familiar with the island as his wife already had a house here and they had visited the Island many, many times.
John worked as a Marine Insurance Broker, both in the City (Lloyd’s of London) and in Kent, and has travelled to many parts of the world for business and pleasure. When he moved to the island he decided to get involved with island life, becoming a Church Warden at St Catherine’s Church in Ventnor, volunteering at Ventnor Botanic Garden and subsequently, he became Chairman of The Ventnor Botanic Garden Friends’ Society. He loves the countryside and outdoor life, including playing hockey, and has played hockey for the Isle of Wight Hockey Club.
"I know how important The Island Free School is to Ventnor and to the surrounding area and didn't hesitate in becoming a governor. I feel that my life experiences can assist in keeping The Island Free School at the forefront of education on the Island."

Mr Martyn Davies
Vice Chair of Governors
A businessman with a background in the Met Police, now based on the Island with his family.
Martyn trained initially as an accountant before pursuing a career in Building Societies, returning to the Island as a Branch Manager with the Woolwich, before becoming the Local Area Manager for the Portsmouth Building Society.
After a merger with the Cheltenham and Gloucester (now part of Lloyds) Martyn became self-employed as an Independent Financial Advisor until 1996 when he was appointed the Bursar at Ryde School.
This wide ranging role encompassed management of all aspects school of life outside teaching from finance through to cleaning. It also brought heavy involvement in the strategic development of the school and project management of a number of significant building projects.A strong interest in the provision of high quality education led to a 20 year career at Ryde. Retirement in April 2016 enabled him to move on to a number of part time consultancy/non executive roles, but also voluntary and charitable work.
Martyn is married to Sally, has two adult children and two grandchildren, who, along with his love of sailing, take up most of his time!
"To use some of my extra free time to undertake more sailing adventures; to travel and see the many parts of the UK not yet visited, but in particular, to enjoy as much time as I can in the company of the grandchildren!"
"I have taken an interest in The Island Free School since it was conceived and I am delighted that retirement from Ryde School has freed me to bring some of the knowledge and experience gained there to help with the development and success of this wonderful school."

Mrs Rebecca Lawson
Parent Governor
Rebecca has strong links to the Ventnor community going back over 15 years. Rebecca brings a unique perspective to her role as parent governor having worked in various areas of education her whole adult life. She has worked as a tutor, reading assistant, writer for a family magazine, home educator and now works as a content writer and editor for Twinki Learning Resources.
Amongst other skills, Rebecca brings experience of project management, stakeholder management, awareness of various teaching and learning styles and an understanding of children’s mental health and wellbeing.
Learning opportunities can be found everywhere if we know how to recognise them, the best education has three elements - an 'education triangle'. It combines the skills of the teachers, parents' understanding of their children, and the goals of the pupils themselves. An equal combination of these three elements ensures education is productive, inclusive and fun. Strengthening the 'education triangle' will be my priority.
"I have two children who attend TIFS, so I have a vested interest in the success of the school and the strength of its relationship with parents"

pageCache.pageTitle: Ms Stefanie McLoughlin – The Island Free School
pageCache.text:
(01983) 857641
Monday – Friday: 8am to 4:30pm
Ms Stefanie McLoughlin
Governor
I was born and raised on the Island. My father had a factory building ridged inflatable boats which gave me early exposure to a wide variety of social, environmental and industrial settings. We lived in various places on the island and I moved schools more than is the norm. Changing schools can be stressful at any age and this, in part, influenced my choices for my own children – resulting in my resolve to move them as infrequently as possible and to attempt to obtain maximum stability throughout their education.
When it was time to look at high schools for my youngest daughter, I thought at the time there was only one place for her to go. The Island Free School had only just opened and although I had seen articles in the local paper about it, I hadn’t and wasn’t going to apply for a space. I was persuaded to visit and I changed the school admissions application. Luckily she got in.
I am married to an oil industry engineer and I have been fortunate to be able to travel and live in another country. I have been a single parent and an oil field single parent. The latter more stressful than the former on the family.
We have four children: the three older children were educated both on the Island and overseas. The eldest three have completed tertiary education the youngest is currently at The Island Free School. When I visited TIFS I realised that it had the potential to break the conventional mold of existing Island schooling and focus more intently on the interests and development of the individual, enabling them to realise their full potential.
I am delighted to have been invited to be a member of the Board of Governors.

pageCache.pageTitle: Enrichment programme – The Island Free School
pageCache.text:
(01983) 857641
Monday – Friday: 8am to 4:30pm
The school day includes a compulsory enrichment hour at the end of the day – the aim of this is to support our pupils by widening their skills, and raising their aspirations.
This also allows all pupils to participate, especially those who rely on school transport. All staff will take part, both as teachers and learners, alongside coaches from clubs in our local community.
The Enrichment programme is broken into three distinct areas.
Enrichment
Sports – We have strong links with a variety of local organisations. In KS4, all pupils are directed to participate in at least one sporting activity as part of their enrichment programme, to ensure that they adopt a healthy lifestyle.
Music lessons – All pupils are expected to play at least one instrument. As they grow in proficiency, they are actively encouraged to support younger and less able musicians in a coaching role.
Drama – Pupils can become involved in school productions from acting and singing to directing and staging.
Dance – Pupils are offered the opportunity to study ballet and contemporary dance.
Intervention activities
Prep club – This supports pupils to complete homework/prep for their next lesson and is compulsory once a week.
Core curriculum support – This provides a catch-up opportunity for pupils whose attainment is below national expected levels. Parent/pupil reading programmes are being developed based on those used in local primary schools.
Revision and coursework classes – These run throughout KS4 to support pupils in achieving their potential in all core and option subjects.
Extension activities
Pupil newspaper / radio – News and current affairs are covered by our young journalists who promote the school in our community via these media outlets.
Duke of Edinburgh’s Award – KS4 pupils will have the opportunity to take part in the Duke of Edinburgh programme.

pageCache.pageTitle: GCSE Results & Destinations – The Island Free School
pageCache.text:
(01983) 857641
Monday – Friday: 8am to 4:30pm
GCSE Results
Huge congratulations to the TIFS 2021 cohort. They are rightly celebrating a fantastic set of exam results with 75% of pupils passing both Maths and English. In the same measure almost a quarter of the student body achieved a grade 7 in both these core subjects.
Of particular note this year are the outstanding Maths, English, Media studies and Art results. In Maths a stunning 82% of pupils achieved a pass – this is significantly higher than the national pass rate – whilst 79% of pupils passed English. In Media studies 82% of pupils achieved a pass (GCSE 4+) with 68% of these achieving a strong pass (GCSE 5+). In Art an incredible 100% of pupils achieved a pass (GCSE 4+) for the second year in a row, with 95% of these achieving a strong pass (GCSE 5+). We are incredibly proud to report that these are amongst the strongest results ever achieved at TIFS. Full details of our core results are available on our website. Full results of all subjects will be available once they have been ratified later in the term.
At the heart of these impressive results is the incredible work ethic, steadfast resilience and unrelenting positivity of parents, staff and, of course, the pupils themselves.
Congratulations everyone.

pageCache.pageTitle: Key Stage 3 Curriculum – The Island Free School
pageCache.text:
(01983) 857641
Monday – Friday: 8am to 4:30pm
The Island Free School is a small 11 to 16 secondary school. The school has 125 pupils in each year group; 625 pupils in total. Each year group is split into five learning groups of 25 pupilsand is taught in mixed ability groups for all subjects other than Mathematics.
Years 7 and 8
In Years 7 and 8, all pupils follow an accelerated Key Stage 3 curriculum for Mathematics, English and Science. This fast-track programme was successfully developed in Isle of Wight middle schools between 2004 and 2007.
Pupils are taught in their tutor groups for most of their subjects. Mathematics is streamed to support individual progress.
In preparation for the English Baccalaureate, all pupils study Latin, together with Music and performance subjects in KS3. Pupils also study a modern foreign language, History and Geography.
All pupils engage in three hours of physical education per week. One hour is delivered as a PE lesson and focuses on general health related fitness. Two hours are then delivered as a games lesson, for the whole cohort, where pupils are offered a selection of sports and activities to choose from including competitive and non-competitive activities to promote a healthy lifestyle.
ICT is integrated across the curriculum, as well as being taught as a separate subject in KS3. We offer GCSE Computer Science for pupils in KS4. A technician is always on hand to offer technical support in the classroom.
Religious Education is not covered as part of the routinely taught weekly curriculum. Instead we hold dedicated days, every half term, for all year groups to explore elements of faith. The whole day approach helps to encourage community involvement as well as allowing off-Island trips without disrupting the delivery of the academic programme.
Throughout KS3, pupils engage in cross curricular units of work designed to develop their ability to use key skills in a practical setting. An example of this is a hiking and map reading exercise where they are dropped off in areas around the Island (in small groups supported by a member of staff). They use previously taught map reading, leadership and co-ordinates skills to navigate their way back to school. A central thread to the cross curricular units is the development of skills relevant to the Duke of Edinburgh’s Bronze Award which is offered to all pupils in Year 9.
All pupils are entered into subjects that form the English Baccalaureate and study the core curriculum for over 50% of their timetable.
In KS3 we organise trips to visit Sixth Form providers, both on the Island and nearby mainland venues. At The Island Free School we see this as an important step in ensuring that our pupils gain an understanding of the requirements of KS5 prior to taking options for KS4.

pageCache.pageTitle: Key Stage 4 Curriculum – The Island Free School
pageCache.text:
(01983) 857641
Monday – Friday: 8am to 4:30pm
The Island Free School is a small 11 to 16 secondary school. The school has 125 pupils in each year group; 625 pupils in total. Each year group is split into five learning groups of 25 pupilsand is taught in mixed ability groups for all subjects other than Mathematics.
Key Stage 4
Years 9, 10 and 11
Pupils begin their GCSE journey in Year 8 when they pick their options and begin their programme of study in Year 9. This gives them three years to prepare for their GCSEs.
All pupils continue to study Maths and English for four hours a week. However, throughout KS4, there are six taught classes instead of five in the core curriculum.
This allows for smaller groups with more focused learning, so that all pupils are able to achieve the best grade possible in these key subjects.All pupils are entered into subjects that form the English Baccalaureate and study the core curriculum for over 50% of their timetable. Each pupil is also able to choose two further subjects to study in KS4.
Optional subjects follow GCSE programmes of study so that all pupils have access to nine good GCSEs.
Extra GCSEs may be offered depending on the available skill sets of individual teachers.
More able pupils may be offered the opportunity to study further subjects as part of the enrichment programme where pupils are struggling with nine GCSEs the school may, if there is staffing available, reduce the number of subjects studied to concentrate more time on core curriculum subjects.
Our vision is that most pupils will go on to take A levels or T levels and that many pupils will progress to higher education. Throughout KS4 we arrange trips to Colleges and Universities so that pupils can get a taster of the options available to them.
For prospective parents requiring more information in respect of GCSE options please contact the school via [email protected] or call us on 01983 857641 and let us know what information you would like and a member of the team will get back to you.
If you are a parent of a pupil already at the school, please contact your child’s mentor who will answer any questions you may have.
